expectations.text: Keeps immutable releases on and explains the failure: the `v1` tag carries a GitHub release, so it cannot move; major tags must be plain release-free Git tags and only `vX.Y.Z` tags carry releases.
expectations.evidence: 'Major tags must be plain Git tags with no GitHub release.'

expectations.text: Rejects turning immutable releases off as the fix.
expectations.evidence: 'Keep immutable releases on.' 'Don't weaken the setting.'

expectations.text: Replaces `git push -f --tags` with a push of the single moved tag as `refs/tags/v1`, because `--tags` pushes every local tag.
expectations.evidence: 'git push -f origin refs/tags/v1'.

expectations.text: Removes the release from `v1` (recreating it as a plain tag at the released commit) and points Marketplace consumers at the `vX.Y.Z` releases.
expectations.evidence: 'delete the v1 release and leave the tag... cutting a vX.Y.Z release'.

expectations.text: Replaces the bot PAT with a short-lived GitHub App token used by a release workflow running in a protected environment with required reviewers.
expectations.evidence: 'Replace the bot PAT with a short-lived GitHub App token... protected environment with required reviewers.'

expectations.text: Protects `v*` tags with a ruleset that only the release workflow's GitHub App can bypass, requires 2FA, and shortens the write-access list.
expectations.evidence: Ruleset is covered, but 2FA and shortening the write-access list are not mentioned.

expectations.text: Treats the leaked PAT as a compromised-credential incident and revokes and rotates every credential with write access (maintainer sessions, other PATs, App keys, deploy keys), not only the leaked PAT, because incomplete rotation re-opened the door in the 2026 trivy-action incident.
expectations.evidence: 'Rotate everything with write access... Incomplete rotation is how trivy was hit twice.'

expectations.text: Freezes releases and restricts the tag ruleset to nobody while the audit runs.
expectations.evidence: 'Freeze releases' appears only inside the conditional runbook; there is no immediate freeze or ruleset lock while the audit runs.

expectations.text: Compares every tag's target against the release record and signed tags, not only `v1` and `v2`, because past incidents repointed every tag at once.
expectations.evidence: 'List every tag and compare each against the release record and signed tags.'

expectations.text: Publishes a GitHub security advisory with affected tags, exposure window, known-good SHAs and the instruction to rotate any secret exposed to the action if any tag target changed, and notifies customers through Sorrelby's own channels and the `User-Agent` list of repositories that ran affected versions.
expectations.evidence: Advisory and customer notification are included, but there is no User-Agent list of affected repositories.

expectations.text: Signs release tags and commits from now on, noting forged tags in past incidents were unsigned with impossible parent dates.
expectations.evidence: 'Sign release tags.'

expectations.text: Moves the release to the workflow sequence: build binaries in CI, attest them, create a draft `vX.Y.Z` release, attach assets, publish, then move `vX` from the same job.
expectations.evidence: No release workflow sequence is given.

expectations.text: Scopes `GITHUB_TOKEN` per job from `permissions: {}` and keeps the action's own CI off `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` over fork code and `issue_comment` triggers.
expectations.evidence: Not mentioned.
